hypothesis: QTXMA is compatible with a bounded double-columnar-transposition model that generalizes from a training prefix to an unscored held-out suffix.
refuted_by: The positive control must be recovered first. If it is, the target still fails unless at least two seeds improve the held-out suffix and the median target gain exceeds the monoalphabetic-substitution control by the preregistered margin.
notes: This is a bounded smoke experiment, not an exhaustive double-transposition exclusion.
Only adjacency n-grams from the existing transparent bootstrap scorer are optimized; monogram frequencies are excluded because transposition preserves them.
Candidate keys are selected using only the first 75 percent of each proposed plaintext. The suffix score is computed only after selection.
The target widths are a small first-pass set centered on short hand-cipher keys and do not include every historically possible rectangle.
A score-only candidate is not an accepted break without coherent plaintext, historical procedure, and independent reproduction.
